items.reasons: B directly preserves the reviewable nested contract, coordinator integration, and unchanged enclosing native actions. A correctly attributes the installer, but leaving root guidance and actions to the coordinator could imply permission to modify them; it does not retain the explicit no-change constraint. B therefore better preserves intended behavior for both clients. This judgment follows the emphasis on explicit instructions in [Claude guidance](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices) and instruction-file sensitivity in [OpenAI guidance](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/latest-model); it is an inference, not a measured model comparison.

sources.quote:
worktree-root guidance and actions, so this bounded application retains the
reviewable nested contract for the coordinator to integrate without modifying
the enclosing repository's native actions.
"nested_project_contract": "validated against installed project-readiness contract validator; enclosing worktree actions not modified",

The nested [project contract](project-contract.json) supplies actual setup, run,
test and verify commands for native Codex/Claude integration. The enclosing
repository's global actions were not modified by this bounded contribution.
Claude responds well to clear, explicit instructions.
It can be more sensitive to instructions contained in skills and other files, such as `AGENTS.md`.
